title: Development and evaluation of school-based back education programs for primary and secondary schools
summary:
This study investigates whether a four-week school-based back training program can improve children’s posture, mobility, and strength. It also examines whether students gain knowledge about back health and change their physical activity behavior.
The program includes simple exercises and educational lessons about the back. Outcomes are assessed before and after the program using tests and questionnaires.
conditions: Back pain and postural abnormalities in children and adolescents, including associated functional limitations.

interventions.name: Students participate in a four-week school-based back education program. The program includes one physical education session and one theoretical lesson per week. In addition, students receive daily exercise cards with specific exercises to strengthen the abdominal and trunk muscles.
Students continue their regular school curriculum for four weeks without any additional back training program.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Students in the 3rd grade at Neustadt an der Donau Primary School and the 5th grade at Anton-Balster Secondary School in Neustadt an der Donau
Exclusion criteria:
Acute orthopedic conditions, acute injuries, contraindications to physical activity, and lack of parental consent.
